question.problem: A spherical hot air balloon is being inflated. At a particular moment, the rate of increase in the volume of the balloon is numerically equal to four times the rate of increase in its surface area. What is the radius of the balloon at that moment?
question.worked_solution:
Let $r$ be the radius of the sphere, $V$ the volume, and $A$ its surface area. We wish to find $r$ at the moment when $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=4\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}.$

To start, let's set up an equation relating the volume $V$ and the surface area $A$ of the sphere. Since $A=4\pi {r}^{2}$ and $V=\frac{4\pi }{3}{r}^{3},$ the relationship between $V$ and $A$ is

$$
V=\frac{4\pi }{3}{r}^{3}=\frac{4\pi }{3}{(\frac{A}{4\pi })}^{3/2}=\frac{{A}^{3/2}}{3(4\pi )^{1/2}}=\frac{{A}^{3/2}}{6\sqrt{\pi }}.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(V) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{A}^{3/2}}{6\sqrt{\pi }}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}A}(\frac{{A}^{3/2}}{6\sqrt{\pi }}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{{A}^{1/2}}{4\sqrt{\pi }}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=4\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{{A}^{1/2}}{4\sqrt{\pi }} \\ {A}^{1/2} & =16\sqrt{\pi } \\ A & ={(16\sqrt{\pi })}^{2} \\ A & =256\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, since $A=4\pi {r}^{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4\pi {r}^{2} & =256\pi  \\ {r}^{2} & =64 \\ r & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
